messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — high CPU on tokenizer-preproc pods in us-west1, multiple OOMKilled events and pod terminations. Runbook: <https://redwood/runbooks/tokenizer-preproc>|tokenizer-preproc
Alex (oncall): seeing it, pulling logs now. cpu spike -> pods being evicted.
Alex (oncall): `kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=tokenizer -o wide` shows 5/10 pods Restarting/CrashLoopBackOff, host nodes with high load.
Samir: throwing up the Grafana panel — CPU per pod, pod restarts.
Marta: are we seeing CUDA errors or pure CPU OOM?
Alex (oncall): logs show repeated OOMKilled from kernel (user-space):
```
Out of memory: Kill process 3421 (tokenizer-preproc) total-vm:1200000kB, anon-rss:980000kB
Killed process 3421 (tokenizer-preproc) total-vm:1200000kB, signal 9 (OOM)
```
And a few serving runtime traces indicating heavy prompt-parsing loops: `tokenize_tokenize_worker()` hot loop.
Priya: Also seeing `cudaMalloc` failures on one GPU node earlier, then node flapped. Node messages: `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` followed by kubelet marking node NotReady. But majority of evictions are CPU OOM on tokenizer containers.
infra-bot: Node events for `gke-us-west1-pool-3-abc`: Kernel OOM, kubelet evicting pods, node restarted at 1999990120.
Alex (oncall): customer-impact check: querying request logs for /v1/generate between 1999990000-1999990200 — 1.7k 500s, 9.2k increased latency >2s. Lee (CS): pinging top customers in case-by-case — some flaky calls reported.
Marta: immediate mitigation I propose: 1) scale tokenizer deployment to +30% CPU limit -> reduce OOMs, 2) apply temporary global rate-limit at edge for heavy prompt paths, 3) cordon affected nodes, 4) roll restart tokenizer with `TOKENIZER_MAX_PARALLELISM=2` env override.
Samir: I can flip rate-limit at API gateway now — applying `--rate-limit 120r/s` for /v1/generate in prod-edge, want me to proceed?
Alex (oncall): do it. Also patch helm values: `resources.requests.cpu: 1000m -> 1200m` and `resources.limits.cpu: 2000m -> 2500m` for tokenizer temporarily.
Priya: pushing a hotfix chart with `env: TOKENIZER_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=30` and `TOKENIZER_MAX_PARALLELISM=2`. Will open PR and ship on-call patch.
Alex (oncall): commands I'm running:
```
kubectl cordon gke-us-west1-pool-3-abc
kubectl drain gke-us-west1-pool-3-abc --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kubectl scale deploy/tokenizer-preproc -n inference --replicas=14
helm upgrade inference -f ci/hotfix-tokenizer-values.yaml inference-chart --namespace inference
```
Marta: good. Also add an emergency autoscaler override to add 3 nodes in the pool (node count +3) while we stabilize.
infra-bot: GKE resize request submitted for pool gke-us-west1-pool-3 (+3 nodes). Estimated add ETA ~4m.
Alex (oncall): applied gateway rate-limit. Watching error-rate graph.
Samir: after rate-limit applied, 500s dropped by ~70% for top endpoints. CPU on tokenizer pods still high but fewer new restarts.
Priya: hotfix helm deployed at 1999990205. New pods come up with lower parallelism and higher mem requests.
Alex (oncall): verifying pod states: `kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=tokenizer -o wide` -> restarted pods are stable, restarts trending down.
Marta: can you confirm there's no single customer pinned to affected nodes? Need to check placement and anti-affinity.
Alex (oncall): placement check: customer A (cs-123) had 70% of requests hitting two tokenizer replicas on affected node earlier; we had no strict anti-affinity for tokenizer preproc.
Lee (CS): notifying impacted customers  — Customer A and Customer D got elevated latency between ~1999990000-1999990200, CS ticket #INC-4881 updated.
Samir: follow-on actions: add pod anti-affinity for tokenizer to spread across nodes, add admission control to reject extremely large prompt batches >1M tokens, and add a circuit-breaker in the gateway per-customer.
Marta: we should add a focused e-2-e test for tokenizer that simulates heavy prompt-parsing loops before promoting. Add to postmortem.
Alex (oncall): quick root-cause hypothesis: a small fraction of prompts triggered pathological tokenizer behavior (regex backtracking + unbounded buffers) on a particular code path. On a couple of nodes there was also a GPU OOM earlier that caused node instability; combined with high CPU bursts, kubelet evicted pods -> cascade.
Priya: created ticket INFRA-2209 to refactor tokenizer loop and clamp memory for tokenization buffers. Linking PRs in the ticket.
infra-bot: node pool resize finished at 1999990248. New nodes draining complete.
Alex (oncall): current status: error-rate down to baseline, restarts <=2 across tokenizer replicas, autoscaler and nodes stable. Customer impact: 2 customers reported incidents, CS opened follow-ups.
Marta: handoff summary for next oncall (Marta takes over in 10m):
- What happened: tokenizer preproc CPU OOMs caused pod evictions and customer-facing 500s. Possible regex/backtrack path.
- Mitigations performed: gateway rate-limit, helm hotfix (lower parallelism + higher mem), cordon/drain affected nodes, scaled replicas and node pool, restarted tokenizer.
- Actions required: INFRA-2209 (tokenizer hardening), add anti-affinity, add admission limit for prompt size, postmortem and customer comms update.
Alex (oncall): leaving a short incident note in #incidents: `<https://redwood/incidents/1999990000>|1999990000 - tokenizer preproc CPU OOM -> pod kills` and assigning INFRA-2209 to Priya.
Lee (CS): customers notified, will send follow-up summary after postmortem.
Marta: thanks team — I'll take oncall. If anything recurs ping me and I'll escalate. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Incident closed for paging at 1999990379, severity lowered to SEV-2, follow-up channel #incidents-postmortem created.
